common_fixes.fix: Set wheelchair_accessible on every trip. If every vehicle is accessible, this may be one default; otherwise use the value for each trip.
Set wheelchair_boarding to 1 (accessible) or 2 (not accessible) for every stop. A field survey can start with the busiest stops.
Add the destination, direction, or 'via' label riders actually see to trip_headsign. Do not copy the route name. If the label changes during the trip, use stop_headsign.
Add fare_attributes.txt (or Fares v2 files) with your fare structure. If your service is fare-free, ask to have it marked fare-free instead.
Remove retired stops from the export, or add them back to the trips that should serve them.
Set wheelchair_boarding to 1 (accessible) or 2 (not accessible) for every terminal. A field survey can start with the busiest terminals.
Re-export with a validity window that reaches at least 60 days out.
Use mixed case for stop names and headsigns (e.g. 'Main St & 2nd Ave', not 'MAIN ST & 2ND AVE').
Re-generate shape_dist_traveled on export so stop and shape distances use the same units.
Check the flagged stops' shape_dist_traveled against the route shape, and re-generate it on export if they disagree.
Re-export the feed with a calendar that reaches further out, and set feed_info feed_end_date past your next service change.
Review the rule documentation for 'block_trips_with_overlapping_stop_times' at https://gtfs-validator.mobilitydata.org/rules.html and check the flagged rows in your feed.
Review the rule documentation for 'same_route_and_agency_url' at https://gtfs-validator.mobilitydata.org/rules.html and check the flagged rows in your feed.
Review the rule documentation for 'missing_required_agency_id' at https://gtfs-validator.mobilitydata.org/rules.html and check the flagged rows in your feed.
Check the flagged stop times for transposed minutes.

comparison.note: Score aggregates and named changes use one current producer contract, raw reader archive profile, and measured-category set across canonical feed records, with unresolved duplicate identities removed. Absolute rankings and individual percentiles are not published.
